title: Developmental Canalization and Context Expression Model
research_questions: Does a latent neurodevelopmental lateralization state predict later hand preference and performance?
Do common and rare variants relate to that state through brain asymmetry?
Does cultural/task exposure alter preference more than performance?
Can the model explain a right-hand majority while preserving minority phenotypes?

hypotheses.claim: A repeated multitask latent phenotype is more reliable and predictive than writing hand alone.
Polygenic and rare coding burden explain small incremental variance in latent developmental lateralization after covariate and family adjustment.
Multivariate brain asymmetry partially mediates genetic liability to later motor phenotype without requiring one cortical location.
Cultural/task exposure shifts preference and writing hand more than bilateral motor-performance asymmetry, with moderation by latent liability.
Latent developmental stability increases with age while task-specific preference remains more plastic.
The direction of the model generalizes across independent cohorts and ancestry groups even if effect sizes differ.

cohorts.discovery: planning target approximately 30000 participants with genotype and harmonizable phenotype
cohorts.prospective: planning target approximately 1500 children followed from 6-18 months through adolescence
cohorts.imaging_nested: planning target approximately 500 participants at ages 8, 12, and 16
cohorts.family_component: twins and siblings where available with zygosity, birth, and forced-switching covariates

formal_model.latent_state: L_it = alpha + beta_g G_i + beta_r R_i + beta_p P_it + u_family + v_site + epsilon_it
formal_model.phenotype: Pr(Y_ijt=k) = softmax_k(lambda_jk L_it + gamma_jk E_ijt + delta_jk L_it E_ijt + c_ijt)
formal_model.mediator: A_it = theta_0 + theta_g G_i + theta_r R_i + theta_p P_it + theta_e E_it + b_i + zeta_it
formal_model.family_sensitivity: Var(L)=A+C+E with forced-switching and birth covariates

analysis.primary: locked discovery construction followed by held-out replication
analysis.secondary: AUC for descriptive comparison only; no diagnostic threshold
analysis.missingness: site-, age-, and cohort-aware missing-data model
analysis.causal_language: association and mediation unless temporal and identification assumptions are met

falsification_rules: genetic terms fail replication or add no variance
culture shifts performance as much as preference
brain mediator fails reliability or cross-site replication
single-task and multitask models are indistinguishable due to classification artifact
unknowns_to_inherit: developmental timing of stable motor asymmetry
effect sizes of common and rare variants
cross-task relation between preference and performance
whether cultural pressure changes latent performance or only expression
